questions.prompt: Name a prophet mentioned by name in the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: There are 25 prophets mentioned by name in the Quran, beginning with Adam and ending with Muhammad ﷺ.

questions.prompt: Name a month of the Islamic calendar
questions.didYouKnow: The Islamic calendar is lunar, so each month begins with the sighting of the new crescent moon. A year is about 11 days shorter than the Gregorian year.

questions.prompt: Name one of the Ten Promised Paradise (al-'Asharah al-Mubashsharah)
questions.didYouKnow: These ten Companions were given the glad tidings of Paradise by the Prophet ﷺ in a single hadith narrated by Sa'id ibn Zayd.

questions.prompt: Name a wife of the Prophet ﷺ (Mothers of the Believers)
questions.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ had eleven wives in total. Khadijah was the only wife who was not a widow or divorcee, and she was his only wife while she lived.

hints.zaynab: Two wives were named Zaynab — Zaynab bint Jahsh and Zaynab bint Khuzaymah. Which did you mean?

questions.prompt: Name a pillar of Iman (Islamic faith)
questions.didYouKnow: The six pillars of Iman come from the hadith of Jibril, where the angel asked the Prophet ﷺ about Iman and he listed them.

questions.prompt: Name an angel mentioned in Islamic tradition
questions.didYouKnow: Jibril (Gabriel) is described in the Quran as the trustworthy spirit (ar-Ruh al-Amin) who brought revelation to the prophets.

questions.prompt: Name one of the last 10 surahs of the Quran (surahs 105–114)
questions.didYouKnow: The last 10 surahs make up most of Juz' 'Amma (the 30th juz'). Al-Ikhlas is said to be worth a third of the Quran.

questions.prompt: Name a surah of the Quran named after an animal
questions.didYouKnow: Al-Baqarah (The Cow) is the longest surah in the Quran with 286 verses. The story of the cow within it involves Bani Isra'il.

questions.prompt: Name a battle or military expedition from the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime
questions.didYouKnow: The Battle of Badr (2 AH) is called 'Yawm al-Furqan' — the Day of Distinction. The Muslims were vastly outnumbered but won a decisive victory.

questions.prompt: Name a compiler of the six major hadith books (Kutub al-Sittah)
questions.didYouKnow: Imam Bukhari is said to have memorised 600,000 hadiths and selected only 7,275 (with repetitions) for his Sahih, calling it the most authentic book after the Quran.

questions.prompt: Name a place mentioned by name in the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: Jerusalem is never named directly in the Quran, but Al-Masjid al-Aqsa (the Farthest Mosque) is mentioned in Surah Al-Isra (17:1).

hints.jerusalem: Jerusalem is not named directly in the Quran, but a mosque there is — Al-Masjid al-Aqsa!
hints.quds: Al-Quds (Jerusalem) is not named in the Quran, but Al-Masjid al-Aqsa is mentioned!

questions.prompt: Name one of the Prophet's ﷺ children
questions.didYouKnow: All of the Prophet's ﷺ sons died in infancy, and Fatimah was the only child to outlive him — though she passed away six months later.

questions.prompt: Name a rite of Hajj or Umrah
questions.didYouKnow: Tawaf al-Ifadah (the main Tawaf of Hajj on the 10th of Dhul Hijjah) is a pillar of Hajj — it cannot be compensated for and must be performed.

hints.tawaf: Great! Which Tawaf — the regular one, Tawaf al-Ifadah, or Tawaf al-Wada'? Just 'Tawaf' counts as the general rite.

questions.prompt: Name a fruit, plant or food mentioned in the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: The fig (Teen) and olive (Zaytun) are sworn by in Surah At-Tin (95:1). Both are considered blessed foods in Islamic tradition.

questions.prompt: Name someone mentioned by name in the Quran who is NOT one of the 25 prophets
questions.didYouKnow: Zayd ibn Harithah is the only Companion of the Prophet ﷺ mentioned by name in the Quran, in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:37).

questions.prompt: Name one of the 5 pillars of Islam
questions.didYouKnow: The five pillars are summarised in a famous hadith: 'Islam is built on five.' They are the foundation of a Muslim's practice.

questions.prompt: Name a Rightly Guided Caliph (al-Khulafa' al-Rashidun)
questions.didYouKnow: The four Rightly Guided Caliphs are all among the Ten Promised Paradise. Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz is sometimes called the fifth due to his just rule.

questions.prompt: Name one of the five daily prayers
questions.didYouKnow: The five daily prayers were established during the Night Journey (Isra' and Mi'raj), when Allah ﷻ first commanded fifty prayers, then reduced them to five at Musa's advice.

questions.prompt: Name a divine scripture revealed to a prophet
questions.didYouKnow: The Suhuf (Scrolls) were revealed to Ibrahim and Musa. Some scholars say Ibrahim received 10 scrolls and Musa 10 more (before the Tawrah).

questions.prompt: Name one of the Ulul 'Azm — the five greatest prophets of firm resolve
questions.didYouKnow: The Ulul 'Azm are mentioned in Quran 46:35 as examples of patience. They are the five who brought the greatest universal messages.

questions.prompt: Name a name or title given to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
questions.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'I have five names: I am Muhammad, Ahmad, Al-Mahi (the Eraser), Al-Hashir (the Gatherer), and Al-'Aqib (the Last).'

questions.prompt: Name one of the seven names of Hell used in the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: Islamic scholars list seven names for Hell in the Quran, each said to refer to a different level or gate of the Fire.

questions.prompt: Name a level or name of Paradise mentioned in Islamic sources
questions.didYouKnow: Al-Firdaws al-A'la (the Highest Firdaws) is said to be directly beneath the Throne of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ advised asking for it specifically.

questions.prompt: Name one of the eight categories eligible to receive Zakat (Surah 9:60)
questions.didYouKnow: The eight categories of Zakat recipients are listed in Surah At-Tawbah (9:60) — the only place in the Quran that explicitly defines who Zakat must go to.

answers.name: New Muslims
aliases: Those whose hearts are to be reconciled

questions.prompt: Name a letter of the Arabic alphabet
questions.didYouKnow: The Arabic alphabet has 28 letters, all consonants. Vowels are indicated by small marks (harakat) written above or below the letters.

questions.prompt: Name a major sign of the Day of Judgement
questions.didYouKnow: The major signs are described in a hadith narrated by Hudhayfah ibn Asid. The scholars say they will occur in rapid succession once they begin.

questions.prompt: Name a famous Quran reciter (qari)
questions.didYouKnow: Sheikh Abdul Basit Abdus Samad (1927–1988) is considered one of the greatest reciters in history. His Mujawwad style set the global standard for Quranic recitation.

questions.prompt: Name a Muslim-majority country
questions.didYouKnow: Indonesia is the world's most populous Muslim-majority country, with over 230 million Muslims — more than the entire Arab world combined.

questions.prompt: Name a founder of a madhhab (Islamic legal school), including extinct ones
questions.didYouKnow: The four surviving madhhabs (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) have hundreds of millions of followers today, though their founders never intended to create separate schools.

questions.prompt: Name a Muslim Premier League footballer
questions.didYouKnow: Mohamed Salah is the first Muslim player to reach 150 Premier League goals. He performs sujud (prostration) after scoring, bringing the gesture to global audiences.

questions.prompt: Name a TV show centred on Muslim characters
questions.didYouKnow: Ramy (2019–) created by Ramy Youssef was praised for its honest portrayal of a first-generation Muslim American navigating faith and identity.

questions.prompt: Name a historic center of Islamic learning or university
questions.didYouKnow: Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco (founded 859 CE) is recognised by UNESCO and the Guinness World Records as the world's oldest continuously operating university.

questions.prompt: Name a word or phrase of dhikr (remembrance of Allah)
questions.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best words are four: SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illa Allah, Allahu Akbar.'

answers.name: La ilaha illa Allah
aliases: There is no god but Allah

answers.name: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
aliases: There is no power except with Allah

questions.prompt: Name any surah (chapter) of the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: The Quran has 114 surahs, the shortest being Al-Kawthar (3 verses) and the longest Al-Baqarah (286 verses).

answers.name: Al-Mumtahanah
aliases: She That Is to Be Examined

questions.prompt: Name a surah from Juz Amma (the 30th and final juz)
questions.didYouKnow: Juz Amma contains 37 surahs (78–114) and is usually the first juz memorised by students of the Quran.

questions.prompt: Name a surah of the Quran that is named after a prophet
questions.didYouKnow: Six surahs are named directly after prophets. Maryam (Mary) also gives her name to a surah, though she is not counted among the 25 named prophets.

questions.prompt: Name a name the Quran gives to itself
questions.didYouKnow: The Quran uses over 50 different names for itself in different verses, the most common being Al-Kitab and Al-Quran.

questions.prompt: Name a name used for the Day of Judgement in the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: The Quran uses over 70 different names for the Day of Judgement, reflecting its many aspects and the awe it inspires.

questions.prompt: Name an animal mentioned in the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: Four surahs are named after animals: Al-Baqarah (Cow), An-Nahl (Bee), An-Naml (Ant), and Al-Ankabut (Spider).

questions.prompt: Name a color explicitly mentioned in the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: Green is the most celebrated color in the Quran, associated with the garments and cushions of Paradise.

questions.prompt: Name a people or nation destroyed by Allah (as mentioned in the Quran)
questions.didYouKnow: These destroyed nations are collectively called the 'Aad al-Ula (the first 'Aad). Their stories are repeated throughout the Quran as warnings.

questions.prompt: Name one of the four stories told in Surah Al-Kahf
questions.didYouKnow: Scholars say reciting Surah Al-Kahf every Friday brings light between the two Fridays, and the first/last 10 verses protect from the Dajjal.

questions.prompt: Name a prophet who is also the son of another prophet (as named in the Quran)
questions.didYouKnow: The Quran mentions several father-son prophetic pairs, with the line of Ibrahim being the most extensive lineage of prophethood.

questions.prompt: Name a miracle of Isa (Jesus) mentioned in the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: The Quran attributes more miracles to Isa than to any other prophet except Muhammad ﷺ, and describes him as the Messiah (Al-Masih).

answers.name: Knowing what people eat and store
aliases: Knowing what people eat and store

questions.prompt: Name one of the plagues or signs sent to Pharaoh's people (as mentioned in the Quran/Surah Al-Araf)
questions.didYouKnow: Surah Al-Araf mentions five of the nine signs sent to Pharaoh. The staff turning into a serpent and the radiant hand are the two signs given to Musa at the outset.

questions.prompt: Name a character (other than Musa himself) from the story of Musa in the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: The story of Musa is the most frequently told story in the Quran, appearing in over 30 different surahs.

answers.name: Samiri
aliases: The one who made the calf

questions.prompt: Name a character (other than Yusuf himself) from the story of Yusuf in the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: Surah Yusuf (chapter 12) is called "the best of stories" (ahsan al-qasas) by the Quran itself.

hints.zulaikha: Zulaikha is a name from tafsir tradition, not the Quran itself. Try a name the Quran actually uses.

questions.prompt: Name a prophet the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ encountered during the Isra' wal-Mi'raj
questions.didYouKnow: During the Night Journey, the Prophet ﷺ met prophets on different levels of the heavens, with Adam in the first heaven and Ibrahim in the seventh.

questions.prompt: Name a ruler or king to whom the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ sent a letter (da'wah letter)
questions.didYouKnow: In the year 628 CE, the Prophet ﷺ sent letters to the rulers of the known world, inviting them to Islam. Heraclius reportedly found the letter compelling.

questions.prompt: Name a grandchild of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ (from his daughter Fatima)
questions.didYouKnow: Hasan and Husayn are described in hadith as the leaders of youth in Paradise. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Hasan and Husayn are my two sweet basil plants in this world.'

hints.zaynab: Two famous Zaynabes — the daughter of Fatima or the daughter of the Prophet ﷺ directly?

questions.prompt: Name an uncle or aunt of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
questions.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ had eight paternal uncles. Only Hamza and Abbas accepted Islam; Abu Lahab is the only person condemned by name in the Quran.

questions.prompt: Name a Companion who served as a scribe of the Quranic revelation
questions.didYouKnow: Over 40 Companions served as scribes of the revelation at various times. Zayd ibn Thabit was the chief scribe and later led the compilation of the Quran under Abu Bakr.

questions.prompt: Name a mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) for the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
questions.didYouKnow: Bilal ibn Rabah, a formerly enslaved Ethiopian, was chosen as the first mu'adhdhin in Islam. He climbed the roof of the Kaaba to call the first adhan after the Conquest of Makkah.

questions.prompt: Name one of the Abadilah — the four great Companions all named Abdullah
questions.didYouKnow: The Abadilah are four Companions who shared the name Abdullah and were all major authorities in Islamic jurisprudence. When scholars said 'Abdullah said…' without qualification, they usually meant one of these four.

questions.prompt: Name a Companion who was tortured for their faith in early Makkah
questions.didYouKnow: Sumayya bint Khayyat is considered the first martyr in Islam, killed by Abu Jahl. Her son Ammar later became a renowned Companion.

questions.prompt: Name a Companion martyred at the Battle of Uhud
questions.didYouKnow: About 70 Companions were martyred at Uhud. The Prophet ﷺ wept deeply over Hamza, calling him 'the master of martyrs.'

questions.prompt: Name a Companion who fought in the Battle of Badr (the first major battle in Islam)
questions.didYouKnow: The Battle of Badr in 624 CE was a turning point. Only 313 Muslims faced ~1000 Qurayshi soldiers. The Prophet ﷺ said the Badr fighters were the best of people.

questions.prompt: Name a Companion who took part in the first migration to Abyssinia (Hijra to Abyssinia)
questions.didYouKnow: In 615 CE, about 15 Companions made the first Hijra to Christian Abyssinia, seeking refuge under the Negus (Ashama ibn Abjar), who refused to hand them over to the Quraysh.

questions.prompt: Name a commander at the Battle of Mu'tah
questions.didYouKnow: At Mu'tah, three commanders were appointed in succession and all three were killed. Khalid ibn al-Walid then took command and conducted a brilliant tactical retreat, earning the title 'Sword of Allah' from the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three Companions who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk
questions.didYouKnow: Their repentance took 50 days. Ka'b ibn Malik's story is one of the most detailed personal accounts in Sirah literature and is recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari.

questions.prompt: Name a Companion known by a famous title (laqab) or honorary name
questions.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ himself gave many Companions their famous nicknames, including calling Khalid 'Sayf Allah' (Sword of Allah) despite Khalid having previously fought against Islam.

answers.name: Abu Hurayrah — Father of the Kitten
aliases: Abu Hurayrah — Father of the Kitten

answers.name: Mus'ab ibn Umayr — Ambassador of Islam
aliases: Mus'ab ibn Umayr — Ambassador of Islam

questions.prompt: Name a hadith collection NOT included in the six major books (Kutub al-Sittah)
questions.didYouKnow: The Muwatta of Imam Malik, compiled around 795 CE, is considered the earliest surviving major hadith collection and was memorised by Imam al-Shafi'i in its entirety.

questions.prompt: Name one of the seven major destructive sins (al-Sab' al-Mubiqat) listed in a hadith
questions.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Avoid the seven destroyers.' This hadith is recorded in both Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.

questions.prompt: Name a type of person who will be under Allah's shade on the Day of Judgement (from the famous hadith of seven)
questions.didYouKnow: This hadith is in both Bukhari and Muslim. Imam al-Nawawi wrote a commentary on it, noting that 'shade' in some narrations refers to the shade of the Throne (Arsh) of Allah.

answers.name: Young person who grew up worshipping Allah
aliases: Young person who grew up worshipping Allah

answers.name: Two people who loved each other for Allah
aliases: Two people who loved each other for Allah

answers.name: Person who remembered Allah and wept
aliases: Person who remembered Allah and wept

questions.prompt: Name a famous scholar of the Tabi'un (the generation after the Companions)
questions.didYouKnow: Said ibn al-Musayyib was considered the greatest of the Tabi'un. He turned down the offer to marry into the Caliph's family, instead marrying the daughter of Abu Hurayrah.

questions.prompt: Name a classical Islamic scholar known for their tafsir (commentary) of the Quran
questions.didYouKnow: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, written in 14th-century Syria, remains one of the most widely read and translated tafsir works in the world.

questions.prompt: Name a branch of traditional Islamic scholarship
questions.didYouKnow: Usul al-Fiqh (principles of jurisprudence) was systematised by Imam al-Shafi'i in his work Al-Risalah, the first book of its kind, written around 820 CE.

questions.prompt: Name a type of voluntary prayer (Sunnah or Nafl) in Islam
questions.didYouKnow: Tahajjud (the night prayer) holds a special status in the Quran; Allah says in Surah Al-Isra: 'And from the night, pray tahajjud as an extra offering for you — perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station.'

questions.prompt: Name a step or act of wudu (ablution)
questions.didYouKnow: Wudu literally means cleanliness and purity in Arabic. The Quran's command for wudu appears in Surah Al-Maidah (5:6), which also describes the steps.

questions.prompt: Name a type of recommended fast beyond the obligatory Ramadan fast
questions.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever fasts six days of Shawwal after Eid al-Fitr will have fasted the entire year.' (Muslim)

answers.name: First nine days of Dhul Hijjah
aliases: First nine days of Dhul Hijjah

questions.prompt: Name one of the four sacred (forbidden) months (al-Ashhur al-Hurum)
questions.didYouKnow: Fighting was forbidden in these four months even in pre-Islamic Arabia. The Quran confirms them in Surah At-Tawbah.

questions.prompt: Name a significant Islamic occasion or celebration on the Islamic calendar
questions.didYouKnow: Laylat al-Qadr (Night of Power) is described in the Quran as 'better than a thousand months.' It falls in the last 10 nights of Ramadan, most likely on an odd night.

questions.prompt: Name one of the 99 Names of Allah (Asma' al-Husna)
questions.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah has 99 names. Whoever memorises them will enter Paradise.' They appear across the Quran and hadith, and their recitation is considered a form of worship.

questions.prompt: Name a sunnah food or remedy mentioned in hadith
questions.didYouKnow: Black seed (Habbatus sawda) is mentioned in a famous hadith: 'In the black seed there is healing for every disease except death.' (Bukhari, Muslim)

questions.prompt: Name a common Islamic phrase or expression (from Quran or Sunnah)
questions.didYouKnow: 'Alhamdulillah' appears 23 times in the Quran. The Prophet ﷺ said it is the best du'a and fills the scales of deeds on the Day of Judgement.

answers.name: La ilaha illallah
aliases: There is no god but Allah

answers.name: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi rajiun
aliases: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi rajiun

answers.name: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
aliases: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah

questions.prompt: Name a sun letter (حرف شمسي) of the Arabic alphabet
questions.didYouKnow: Arabic has 14 sun letters and 14 moon letters. When the definite article 'al' precedes a sun letter, the 'l' assimilates into the following letter — so 'al-shams' is pronounced 'ash-shams'.

questions.prompt: Name a moon letter (حرف قمري) of the Arabic alphabet
questions.didYouKnow: Moon letters keep the 'l' of 'al' silent — so 'al-qamar' is pronounced as written. The word 'qamar' (moon) starts with a moon letter, hence the name.

questions.prompt: Name a letter of the qalqalah (echo) group in Arabic Tajwid
questions.didYouKnow: The five qalqalah letters are remembered by the mnemonic 'قطب جد' (qutb jadd). When one of these letters has sukun (no vowel), it produces a brief bouncing echo sound.

questions.prompt: Name the Arabic word for a number from 1 to 10
questions.didYouKnow: Arabic numerals (the digits 0-9) were actually introduced to Europe from the Islamic world. The word 'algebra' comes from Arabic 'al-jabr', from Al-Khwarizmi's 9th-century book.

questions.prompt: Name a day of the week in Arabic
questions.didYouKnow: The Arabic days of the week are mostly numbered (second day, third day, etc.), except for Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah — Day of Gathering) and Saturday (Yawm al-Sabt — from the Hebrew Shabbat).

questions.prompt: Name an Arabic question word (interrogative)
questions.didYouKnow: 'Man' (who) and 'Ma' (what) are among the first question words learnt. They also appear in Surah Al-Baqarah when the angels asked about Adam: 'Man hadha?'

questions.prompt: Name a standard Arabic greeting or phrase of courtesy
questions.didYouKnow: 'Ahlan wa sahlan' — the classic Arabic welcome — literally means 'you are family, and the land is easy for you.' It signals that the guest is as welcome as family.

questions.prompt: Name a Muslim player who has won the UEFA Champions League
questions.didYouKnow: Zinedine Zidane won the Champions League as both a player (Real Madrid, 2001/02) and a manager (three consecutive times, 2015/16–2017/18).

questions.prompt: Name a Muslim world boxing champion
questions.didYouKnow: Muhammad Ali, born Cassius Clay, converted to Islam in 1964. He said: 'The name Cassius Clay is a slave name. I didn't choose it and I don't want it.'

questions.prompt: Name a nasheed (Islamic vocal music) artist
questions.didYouKnow: Maher Zain's debut album 'Thank You Allah' (2009) has sold over 2 million copies worldwide and has been translated into more than 20 languages.

questions.prompt: Name a member state of the Arab League
questions.didYouKnow: The Arab League was founded in Cairo in 1945 by six states: Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, and Syria. Palestine joined as a member in 1976.

questions.prompt: Name a country that has a crescent symbol on its national flag
questions.didYouKnow: Turkey's crescent and star flag dates back to the Ottoman Empire. The red background represents the blood of the Ottoman army and the crescent is an ancient symbol of the city of Istanbul (Byzantine Byzantium).

questions.prompt: Name a famous mosque outside the two holy cities (Makkah and Madinah)
questions.didYouKnow: The Blue Mosque (Sultanahmet Mosque) in Istanbul has six minarets — a unique feature that caused controversy when built in 1616, as it matched the number of minarets of the mosque in Makkah at the time.

questions.prompt: Name a famous mosque in the United Kingdom
questions.didYouKnow: The East London Mosque, opened in 1985, can accommodate 7,000 worshippers and is one of the largest mosques in Western Europe.

questions.prompt: Name a part of or feature of the Kaaba
questions.didYouKnow: The Black Stone (Hajar al-Aswad) was described by the Prophet ﷺ as a stone from Paradise. It has been broken into several pieces over the centuries and is now held together by a silver frame.

questions.prompt: Name a sweet or dessert from the Muslim world
questions.didYouKnow: Baklava's exact origins are disputed between Turkey, Greece, and the Arab world, but its classic layered-pastry form was perfected in the Ottoman imperial kitchens.

questions.prompt: Name a food traditionally eaten to break the fast (iftar) in Ramadan
questions.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'When one of you breaks the fast, let him break it with dates. And if he can't find any, let him break it with water, for it is purifying.' (Abu Dawud)

questions.prompt: Name an Islamic dynasty or empire
questions.didYouKnow: The Abbasid Caliphate lasted from 750 CE to 1258 CE — over 500 years — making it one of the longest-lasting imperial dynasties in history. It ended when Baghdad was sacked by Hulagu Khan.

questions.prompt: Name an Ottoman Sultan
questions.didYouKnow: Mehmed II conquered Constantinople in 1453 CE at the age of 21, fulfilling the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ: 'You will surely conquer Constantinople. How great is the commander who will conquer it.'

questions.prompt: Name a Muslim scientist from the Islamic Golden Age
questions.didYouKnow: Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen) wrote his Book of Optics around 1011 CE, accurately describing how vision works for the first time. He is widely considered the father of modern optics.

questions.prompt: Name a language that is or was written using the Arabic script
questions.didYouKnow: Urdu and Persian use a modified Arabic script called Nastaliq, which is written at an angle and considered one of the most beautiful calligraphic styles in the world.

questions.prompt: Name a famous Muslim woman from history (pre-20th century)
questions.didYouKnow: Fatima al-Fihri founded the University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco in 859 CE. It is recognised by UNESCO as the world's oldest continuously operating university.
